description: HydroChrono is a hydrodynamic simulation toolkit for wave-energy converters and other offshore multibody systems. Its developers combine Project Chrono dynamics with hydrodynamic coefficients in BEMIO-format HDF5 files, time-domain radiation forces, moorings and a YAML-driven command line. Inputs include device geometry, coefficient files, waves, mooring and simulation settings; outputs are animated motion and portable HDF5 result files. Geography and simulated duration follow the selected device and sea state, with no built-in national data coverage. MIT-licensed source and a prototype release are free on GitHub. The README calls version 0.7 a prototype, but GitHub marks this repository archived as of the review date. Its active-development claim may be stale, and more advanced power-take-off and control are only described as plans. Current hydrodynamic loads are first order, so results require care for strongly nonlinear conditions. HydroChrono can test wave-energy device response and offshore infrastructure performance. The related catalogue data-ihdata-ihcantabria-wave-hindcasts could provide environmental context after format conversion, but no connection was checked. No model archive was downloaded or simulation run.
